## 0. Conventions and imported inputs

k has characteristic zero; geometric points have algebraically closed residue fields of characteristic zero. For a geometric point b write C=C_b, gamma=gamma_b, D=D_b:=gamma^*(pt). Trace splits gamma_*O_C=O+E^vee with E locally free of rank 3 and deg E=g+d-1=9. Put X:=Proj_{P^1}(Sym E), so p_*O_X(m)=Sym^m E.

Hypotheses carried, not proved (FND-0105 discipline):
- (N) fibrewise weak CE normalization O_X(1)|_{C_b} iso omega_{C_b/P^1} tensor gamma_b^*A_b. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 gives deg(O_X(1)|_C)=2g+6=18=deg(omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)); a twist by gamma^*A shifts by 4 deg A, so deg A=0 and A iso O. Hence O_X(1)|_C=omega_{C/P^1}. This is the conclusion of ATT-0066/CLM-0066-2 under (N), confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116.
- (R) the standard degree-four CE ideal resolution as in ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109. Balanced means F iso O(4)+O(5).

Imported dual-confirmed facts, used only inside stated scope:
- ATT-0065/CLM-0065-5 [REV-0108, REV-0109]: fibrewise balanced F carries a canonical O(5)-subbundle inducing 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with degrees 20 and 16, with no global splitting of F.
- ATT-0066/(H1) [REV-0110, REV-0116]: deg L=6, deg M=4, chi(L)=1, h^0(L)=1+h^0(M); under (N), L_b iso omega(-D_b), M_b iso gamma_b^*O(1); h^0(L_b) in {3,4}.
- ATT-0066/(H3) with FND-0107: I is the correct closed Abel-Jacobi model over all of B; over a reduced locally closed constant-h^0 stratum of value k, I is a P^{k-1}-bundle.
- ATT-0066/(H4), FND-0064, FND-0075: Z_ev->I^dist is a finite etale S_6-torsor at stack level, neither side reduced unilaterally.

Degree receipts: deg(W_5)=16, deg(L)=6 [sha256 96775421e0e1440fb7c04fd11e156d83ab93facfaa0ed861bde18398bb5d254e]; deg M=4 [sha256 b81f0e4d2a6c93d7e45b18f067d3a0c90f92e5b4d13c76a884ab50e2f60d19c3]. No working-context row is used as a substitute for proof below.

## 1. CE quadric-count inequality

Lemma 1. Under (N) and (R), on each geometric fibre F iso p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) and

  0 -> F -> Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(omega_{C/P^1}^{tensor 2}) -> 0   (1.1)

is exact on P^1. Hence for every integer m,

  h^0(F(-m)) >= h^0(Sym^2E(-m)) - h^0(C, omega_{C/P^1}^{tensor 2} tensor gamma^*O(-m)).   (1.2)

In particular a nonzero kernel at m=6 refutes balancedness, since O(4)+O(5) twisted by O(-6) is O(-2)+O(-1) with h^0=0.

Proof. Tensor (R) by O_X(2). On a P^2-bundle H^i(P^2,O(-2))=0 for all i, so Rp_*(O_X(-2) tensor p^*det F)=0 and p_*(I_C(2)) iso F with R^1=0. Push 0->I_C(2)->O_X(2)->i_*(O_X(2)|_C)->0 along p, using p_*O_X(2)=Sym^2E, p_*i_*=gamma_*, and O_X(2)|_C=omega_{C/P^1}^{tensor 2} from (N), to get (1.1). Left-exact H^0 after twisting by O(-m) gives (1.2). Rank check 2+4=6; deg Sym^2E=4 deg E=36 and chi(omega_{C/P^1}^2)=31 force deg F=9, matching O(4)+O(5). QED

## 2. Hyperelliptic exclusion

Lemma 2. If C is hyperelliptic of genus 6 and gamma:C->P^1 has degree 4, then F is not balanced.

Proof. Let h:C->P^1 be the hyperelliptic map and A:=h^*O(1).

(2a) Factorization. For psi=(gamma,h):C->P^1 x P^1 with image Z and e:=deg(C->Z), one has e|2. If e=1 then [Z]=2H_1+4H_2 and p_a(Z)=3, contradicting genus 6. Hence e=2, Z iso P^1, and gamma=q o h with deg q=2.

(2b) E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4). One has h_*O_C=O+O(-7). With q^*O(1)=O(2), projection and a twist test give q_*O(-7)=O(-4)^2, so gamma_*O_C=O+O(-1)+O(-4)^2 and E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4). Section counts h^0(mD)=2m+1 for m<=3 independently force the same splitting type.

(2c) Count. Sym^2E(-6) has h^0=9. On the other side omega_C=5A (RR plus h^0(5A)>=6), gamma^*O(1)=2A, so omega_{C/P^1}^2 tensor gamma^*O(-6)=6A of degree 12>10 with h^0=7. By (1.2), h^0(F(-6))>=2, so F is not balanced. QED

## 3. Emptiness of B_4

Proposition 3. Under the Theorem hypotheses, h^0(O(D_b))=2 and h^0(L_b)=3 for every geometric b. Hence B_4 is empty and B=B_3 topologically.

Proof. Balancedness with Lemma 2 excludes hyperelliptic fibres. D has degree 4 and h^0(D)>=2 (gamma^* injective on H^0(O(1))), and h^1(D)=h^0(D)+1>0, so D is special and Clifford gives h^0(D)<=3. Equality forces C hyperelliptic (deg 4 not in {0,10}), excluded. So h^0(D)=2, and ATT-0066/(H1) with M iso O(D) gives h^0(L)=3. QED

Remark (FND-0104). This is exactly the exclusion to which FND-0104 localized GAP-H0-1. Bielliptic factorizations through positive-genus intermediates retain h^0(D)=2 and are not excluded; they appear as case (E)(ii) below. This respects the working-context constraint that constancy of h^0(omega(-D)) is not equivalent to excluding every non-primitive pencil.

## 4. Plane-quintic exclusion

Lemma 4. If C is a smooth plane quintic and gamma:C->P^1 has degree 4, then F is not balanced.

Proof. Write H=O_C(1), so omega_C=2H. C is not hyperelliptic.

(4a) Every degree-four pencil is |H-p|. As in Proposition 3, h^0(D)=2. The base-point-free pencil trick on V=H^0(D) and N=H gives 6<=2h^0(H-D)+4, so h^0(H-D)>=1. Deg(H-D)=1 forces D iso H-p.

(4b) E=O(2)+O(3)+O(4). Section counts h^0(mD) equal 1,2,4,7 for m=0,1,2,3 force the splitting type (2,3,4).

(4c) Seven into six. Generators x_2,x_3,x_4 of the summands of E restrict with x_4|_C cutting exactly 2p (since h^0(2p)=1) and ord_p(x_3|_C)>=1 (since h^0(H+p)=h^0(H)=3). Sym^2E(-6) has h^0=7. All seven basis monomials restrict into H^0(2H+2p) (dimension 7) with order of vanishing at p at least 2, hence into the 6-dimensional subspace H^0(2H) after dividing by the section of O(2p). Nonzero kernel and Lemma 1 refute balancedness. QED

## 5. Base-point-freeness of |L|

Proposition 5. Under the Theorem hypotheses, |L_b| is base-point-free on every geometric fibre.

Proof. By Proposition 3, h^0(L)=3 and C is not hyperelliptic. A point p is a base point iff h^0(D+p)=3. Then D+p is a special g^2_5. A base point of |D+p| would give Clifford equality on a degree-4 system, forcing hyperellipticity, excluded; so |D+p| is base-point-free. The associated morphism C->P^2 is birational onto a plane quintic of arithmetic genus 6, hence an isomorphism, so C is a smooth plane quintic, contradicting Lemma 4. QED

This refutes the carried candidate that L fails to be base-point-free on the balanced locus because of plane-quintic examples: those examples are unbalanced by Lemma 4.

## 6. Components, dimensions, and fibrewise reduced support

Proposition 6. (a) Over reduced B, pi_*L is locally free of rank 3 with base change and I iso P((pi_*L)^vee) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over all of B. (b) Irreducible components of I are the preimages of those of B, of dimension dim(component)+2. (c) On every geometric fibre the reduced-support locus is a dense open of |L_b| iso P^2. (d) I^dist is dense open in I, surjective onto B, with the same components and dimensions; Z_ev->I^dist is a nonempty finite etale S_6-torsor at stack level, equidimensional of the same dimension.

Proof. (a) Constant h^0=3 from Proposition 3 plus Grauert on reduced B (REV-0116/FC-H0-NONREDUCED-GRAUERT) and ATT-0066/(H3) with B_3=B. (b) Projectivized bundles are locally U x P^2. (c) By Proposition 5 the evaluation ker defines a smooth irreducible incidence J of dimension 2 over C mapping dominantly to |L_b| iso P^2; generic smoothness in characteristic zero gives a dense open of reduced (hence six-distinct-point) fibres. The reduced-support locus is open and now nonempty in irreducible P^2, hence dense. chi(L)=1 is not used to produce the reduced member, so the blocked chi(L)=1 route is avoided. (d) Follows from (c) and ATT-0066/(H4). QED

No absolute dimension of B is used. The blocked inference dim(I)=15+k-1 is not made.

## 7. Universal divisor and transitive monodromy

Proposition 7. Over reduced B, K:=ker(pi^*pi_*L->L) is locally free of rank 2, script-D=P(K^vee) over C is a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle, finite locally free of degree 6 over I and etale over I^dist. Components of script-D match those of B. If B is irreducible then the six-point etale monodromy over I^dist has transitive image G and Z_ev has exactly [S_6:G] irreducible components.

Proof. Base-point-freeness makes evaluation surjective, so K has rank 2. The rest is the standard orbit description of a finite etale S_6-torsor over a connected base. QED

## 8. Residual trichotomy and 2-transitivity

Proposition 8. For phi=phi_{L_b}:C->P^2 one has e*deg(Z)=6 with deg Z>=2, so e in {1,2,3}: (i) e=1: plane sextic with p_a=10 and total delta 4; (ii) e=2: smooth plane cubic (rational normalization would be hyperelliptic, excluded), so C bielliptic and L=p^*N of degree 3; (iii) e=3: smooth conic, C trigonal and L=2T. In case (i) the monodromy over |L_b|^dist is 2-transitive.

Proof. Numerology as stated. For 2-transitivity: the ordered double-point incidence J_2 over C x C minus the diagonal has a unique 2-dimensional component dominating a dense open of |L_b|, giving transitive action on ordered pairs; surjectivity of pi_1 of a dense open upgrades to the whole |L_b|^dist. QED

Cases (ii) and (iii) are not excluded; upgrading (i) to G=S_6 needs a transposition and is left open (GAP-COMP-MONODROMY).

## 9. Stabilizers

Proposition 9. (a) If Gamma has at least three distinct gamma-images and one unramified point, then Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)=1. (b) Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)->Aut(C,Gamma) is an isomorphism.
